label: Modal spine A3 against the initial-state view: founded coming-to-be and survival models
summary: Target: premise A3 of the modal spine (possibly, contingent concrete things are absent at a moment and present at a later one) against its recorded rival, the initial-state view (docs/notes/modal-spine.md). Finding 1, a derivation: A3 follows from the single possibility premise that some accessible history has a contingent concrete individual present at a moment with a founded past (no endless descent of moments below it) while every contingent concrete individual of that history comes to be, in the sense of being absent at some strictly earlier moment whenever present (ContingentComingToBe.possibleContingentFreePast). The proof descends to a moment with nothing earlier, where coming to be excludes every contingent occupant. Finding 2, the rival's exact survival conditions: the initial-state view is thereby incompatible with possible founded coming-to-be, and the controls show it survives, without a necessary individual and with inert emptiness intact, in the two ways the derivation leaves open: an endless past in which each contingent thing is preceded by another (integer times, no founded moment), and a founded past whose contingent thing never came to be. So a holder of the rival who denies a necessary concrete being is committed to this: in every possible history, either some contingent concrete thing was never preceded by its own absence, or no populated moment has a founded past. Relation to existing records: the corpus holds that 'each being is at some time not' does not entail 'at some time nothing is' (the Third Way quantifier-shift objection); the present result is valid because it requires an EARLIER absence, a founded past, and restricts the conclusion to contingent concrete things. Nothing is attributed to Aquinas. Rejected approach: a subtraction or recombination principle for A3 (each contingent thing could be absent, so all could be); it yields a possible empty world, which under the spine's frame premises contradicts the conclusion, so it was not encoded. No premise is established.
blocker: The new possibility premise is OPEN and stronger than A3. The two horns the rival is pushed to (never-generated contingent things; an endless past in every possible history) were tested on 2026-11-11 against the Grim Reaper, causal-finitism and brute-foundation results, with a replacement account for each: see the attempt 'Modal spine A3′: pricing the endless-past and never-generated horns of the initial-state view', whose open bridges and next tests carry this blocker forward.
